title: ACME Corp v. WidgetCo — Breach of Supply Agreement
description: ACME Corp alleges WidgetCo materially breached a supply agreement by failing to deliver 10,000 Model-X widgets by March 31, 2024. WidgetCo contends delivery was excused by a force majeure event (government export controls on chip supplier Fab-Taiwan). A secondary dispute concerns whether ACME made a prepayment of $125,000 before the alleged breach date.

claims.statement: ACME Corp made NO payment to WidgetCo prior to the alleged breach date of March 31, 2024.
claims.reason: EV-002 explicitly records a $125,000 prepayment received by WidgetCo on January 20, 2024 — directly contradicting the claim.

claims.statement: WidgetCo's delivery delay was excused by a valid force majeure event (government export controls on Fab-Taiwan).
claims.reason: EV-001 contains the force majeure clause (§9.3); EV-002 shows timely force majeure notice; EV-003 is expert testimony authenticating the government notice and confirming no reasonable alternative.

legal_questions: Did WidgetCo materially breach the supply agreement?
Is the force majeure clause in §9.3 applicable to the government export control event?
What damages, if any, does ACME Corp owe or is owed?
